mechanism_narrative: A sustained multi-week rise in WORKPLACES mobility (from -34.3 to -27.4) signals resuming commuting routines, which spill over into weekday retail and recreation footfall, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise (mean next 28d <= mean last 28d) despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend through the forecast window.

mechanism_narrative: A cumulative decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -9.3 to -16.4 over three weeks) indicates growing household caution about non-essential errands; once this decline crosses a severity threshold it generalizes to discretionary retail trips, pulling RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains below -15% for the subsequent two weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES rising and TRANSIT remaining flat, invalidating the proposed substitution mechanism.
